name: AD8510 / AD8512 / AD8513
tagline: ADI's 8 MHz JFET dual with 8 nV/√Hz and 0.0005% THD+N; one Chinese DIY report likens it to the AD823 in headphone amps.

lineage.note: Sole source. Introduction year unconfirmed. Early editions covered AD8510/AD8512 only; AD8513 quad added later.
PCN 25_0156 moves AD8510/AD8512/AD8513 to an existing qualified process at ADI's Camas, WA fab.

part_numbers.note: Single; A/B offset grades, SOIC-8 (R) and MSOP-8 (RM). Orderables and status unconfirmed.
Dual, ADI 'Production'. ARZ confirmed; ARMZ (MSOP-8) and BRZ (tighter Vos) unconfirmed.
Older non-RoHS codes without Z suffix; probably obsolete (unconfirmed).
Quad, added to the datasheet later. SOIC-14 / TSSOP-14 (unconfirmed). Status unconfirmed.
Enhanced Product (defense/aerospace) dual with its own datasheet.

reputation.summary: A niche reputation. The main praise is one post in an erji.net thread on op-amps the poster has used: it sounds almost like the AD823, with more output current and lower supply current, slightly harsh but 'not unpleasant', and suits headphone amps. No wider consensus in Western forums is known.
typical_uses: Op-amp swaps in DIY headphone amplifiers
Low-noise JFET-input audio gain stages (inferred from specs)
caveats: Praise comes from a single forum post; do not generalise.
Needs at least ±5 V (about 10 V total); output is not rail-to-rail.
SMD only (SOIC/MSOP/TSSOP); DIP sockets need an adapter.
JFET bias current roughly doubles every 10 °C; keep it away from hot spots.

counterfeit_notes: No family-specific counterfeit reports. As a mid-price SMD-only ADI JFET part, relabelled or reclaimed marketplace units are a generic risk. Buy from authorised distributors and check ADI marking and date codes.

silicon_changes.summary: Wafer-fab change: listed AD8510/AD8512/AD8513 part numbers move to an existing qualified process at ADI's Camas, WA fab to ensure supply. ADI expects no fit, form, function or reliability impact. Previous fab not stated. Datasheet unchanged (Rev. K).
silicon_changes.identification: No date-code or trace-code cutover known; check the PCN's effective date and date codes.
silicon_changes.audio_impact: None claimed; datasheet limits unchanged. Typical noise, bias and offset distributions could shift within limits (unverified).
silicon_changes.compatibility_risk: low: same part numbers and datasheet limits; vendor states no fit/form/function change
silicon_changes.verification: PCN form text confirmed; previous fab and dates not established.

claims_confirmed: Current ADI datasheet is AD8510/AD8512/AD8513 Rev. K (https://www.analog.com/media/en/technical-documentation/data-sheets/ad8510_8512_8513.pdf).

PCN 25_0156 moves AD8510/AD8512/AD8513 to an existing qualified Camas, WA process, no expected fit/form/function impact (https://mm.digikey.com/Volume0/opasdata/d220001/medias/docus/7560/ADI_PCN_25_0156_Rev_-_Form.pdf).
8 MHz GBW, 20 V/µs, 7.6 nV/√Hz at 10 kHz, 0.0005% THD+N; AD8512 in Production (https://www.analog.com/en/products/ad8512.html).
Front page: 8 nV/√Hz, 400 µV max Vos, 1 µV/°C, 25 pA, 500 ns settling, ±5 to ±15 V (https://www.analog.com/media/en/technical-documentation/data-sheets/ad8510_8512_8513.pdf).
An early 'AD8510/AD8512'-only edition is mirrored by RS (https://docs.rs-online.com/17b1/0900766b801ce1ae.pdf).
